assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific light behavior (reflection causing a sun pillar) but does not support the guided exploration of light sources, how light behaves or can be changed, or its everyday uses as required by G3-F-6. It is a factual description of an atmospheric phenomenon, not an activity or explanation tied to the competency's scope.

copy.en:
What is a sun pillar?

It is a vertical streak of light above or below the sun! It appears when light reflects off tiny flat ice crystals floating in the air.
copy.tl:
Ano ang sun pillar?

Ito ay isang patayong guhit ng liwanag sa itaas o ibaba ng araw! Lumilitaw ito kapag ang sinag ay naaaninag sa mga maliliit na patag na kristal ng yelo sa hangin.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang sun pillar?

Usa kini ka tindog nga linya sa kahayag sa ibabaw o ilawom sa adlaw! Motungha kini kung ang silaw mabanaag sa gagmay nga patag nga mga kristal sa yelo nga naglutaw sa hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Our Sun sits in one of the Milky Way's spiral arms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Sun's location within the Milky Way galaxy, not the structure of the solar system, its major celestial objects, their features, or composition. It shares the topic of the Sun but does not directly support the competency's focus on the solar system.

copy.en: Our Sun sits in one of the Milky Way's spiral arms, living far away from its bright center!
copy.tl: Ang ating Araw ay matatagpuan sa isang braso ng Milky Way, malayo sa maliwanag na sentro nito!
copy.bis: Ang atong Adlaw nahimutang sa usa sa mga braso sa Milky Way, layo sa hayag nga sentro niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Solar energy drives evaporation and transpiration
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes solar energy driving evaporation and transpiration in the water cycle. It does not address pushes/pulls changing speed or direction of objects, which is the focus of G4-F-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Solar energy drives evaporation and transpiration
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the water cycle, not about planning an investigation into friction on different surfaces. It provides no support for G5-F-2.

copy.en: Solar energy drives evaporation and transpiration, moving water from the earth's surface and from plant leaves up into the atmosphere.
copy.tl: Ang enerhiya ng araw ang nagpapatakbo ng evaporation at transpiration, na nag-aangat ng tubig mula sa lupa at mula sa mga dahon papunta sa atmosphere.
copy.bis: Ang enerhiya sa adlaw mao ang nagpalihok sa evaporation ug transpiration, nga nagpataas sa tubig gikan sa yuta ug sa mga dahon paingon sa atmosphere.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without the Sun's gravitational force
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the Sun's gravitational force holding heavenly bodies, not friction, heat production, or reducing/increasing friction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without the Sun's gravitational force
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that work is done when a force causes the displacement of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address work being done when a force causes displacement; it only mentions gravitational force keeping bodies in place.

copy.en: Without the Sun's gravitational force, all heavenly bodies would fly in different directions and may even collide with each other.
copy.tl: Kung wala ang gravitational force ng Araw, ang lahat ng heavenly bodies ay lilipad sa iba't ibang direksyon at maaaring magbanggaan pa sa isa't isa.
copy.bis: Kung wala ang gravitational force sa Adlaw, ang tanang heavenly bodies molupad sa lain-laing direksyon ug mahimong magbangga sa usag-usa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun is the principal driver of Earth's climate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the Sun's role in climate and solar radiation, with no mention of separating mixtures or any technique such as decantation, filtering, or sieving. It is entirely unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun is the principal driver of Earth's climate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the benefits of each mixture separation technique in preparing useful products
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address mixture separation techniques or their benefits in preparing useful products. It is about climate and solar energy, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: The Sun is the principal driver of Earth's climate because its energy powers life and drives solar radiation, solar energy absorption, seasonal variations, solar cycles, and solar variability.
copy.tl: Ang Araw ang pangunahing nagtutulak ng climate ng Earth dahil ang energy nito ang nagpapagana sa buhay at nagtutulak ng solar radiation, solar energy absorption, seasonal variations, solar cycles, at solar variability.
copy.bis: Ang Adlaw mao ang pangunang nagduso sa climate sa Earth tungod kay ang energy nagpalihok sa kinabuhi ug nagduso sa solar radiation, solar energy absorption, seasonal variations, solar cycles, ug solar variability.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At noon, the sun is high and your shadow is super short! In the morning or afternoon, the sun is lower and your shadow stretches out long.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes shadow length changes with sun height but does not mention direction, a shadow stick, or infer why the Sun changes position, which are core parts of the competency.

copy.en: At noon, the sun is high and your shadow is super short! In the morning or afternoon, the sun is lower and your shadow stretches out long.
copy.tl: Sa tanghali, mataas ang araw at super maikli ang anino mo! Sa umaga o hapon, mababa ang araw at humahaba ang anino mo.
copy.bis: Sa udto, taas ang adlaw ug super mubo ang imong landong! Sa buntag o hapon, ubos ang adlaw ug mahaba ang imong landong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a sudden, powerful burst of energy and light from the Sun's surface
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a solar flare, a transient explosive event, not the Sun's overall characteristics such as composition, size, or main radiated energy. It shares the Sun topic but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a sudden, powerful burst of energy and light from the Sun's surface
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions energy and light but does not identify energy as something that can cause change, nor does it address light, sound, or heat energy as forms of energy. It is only topically related.

copy.en:
What is a solar flare?

It's a sudden, powerful burst of energy and light from the Sun's surface, usually near sunspots! It's one of the biggest explosions in our Solar System.
copy.tl:
Ano ang solar flare?

Ito ay biglaang malakas na pagsabog ng energy at light sa ibabaw ng Araw, kadalasan malapit sa sunspots! Isa ito sa pinakamalakas na explosion sa Solar System.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang solar flare?

Kini usa ka kalit ug kusog nga pagbuto sa energy ug light gikan sa nawong sa Adlaw, kasagaran duol sa sunspots! Usa kini sa pinakakusog nga explosion sa Solar System.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: continuous stream of charged particles (ions and electrons) released by the Sun
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes solar wind as charged particles released by the Sun, which touches on the Sun's composition and radiation, but it does not describe the Sun's overall characteristics such as size or main energy radiated (light/heat). The focus is on a specific phenomenon, not the Sun's general properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: continuous stream of charged particles (ions and electrons) released by the Sun
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun and Earth but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their features and composition. Solar wind is a solar phenomenon, not a description of the solar system's structure.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When they reach Earth, they create beautiful auroras near the poles.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how natural objects in the sky affect activities of people
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions auroras created by solar wind, which could be seen as an effect on people's activities (e.g., viewing auroras), but it does not explain how natural objects in the sky affect activities of people in a general sense. The connection is too indirect and not the card's main instructional focus.

copy.en:
What is the solar wind?

It's a continuous stream of charged particles (ions and electrons) released by the Sun in all directions! When they reach Earth, they create beautiful auroras near the poles.
copy.tl:
Ano ang solar wind?

Ito ay patuloy na daloy ng charged particles (ions at electrons) na pinalalabas ng Araw sa lahat ng direksyon! Pagdating sa Earth, gumagawa sila ng magagandang aurora sa mga polo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang solar wind?

Kini usa ka padayon nga agos sa charged particles (ions ug electrons) nga ginapagawas sa Adlaw sa tanang direksyon! Kung moabot sa Yuta, naghimo kini og matahum nga aurora duol sa mga poste.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: staring at the sun is super damaging
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that UV and infrared light from the sun harm the retina and that staring at the sun is damaging, but it does not describe any safety measures (e.g., wearing sunglasses, avoiding direct eye contact, using shade). The warning is implicit at best, not an explicit description of protective actions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: These can harm your retina cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how light and sound can be harmful to people and make suggestions on how to protect oneself from them
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that invisible UV and infrared light can harm retina cells, which is an example of light being harmful. However, it does not explain how light and sound can be harmful generally, nor does it make suggestions on how to protect oneself. The harm is mentioned but the protective suggestions are absent.

copy.en: The sun gives off invisible ultraviolet (UV) and infrared light. These can harm your retina cells, which is why staring at the sun is super damaging!
copy.tl: Naglalabas ang araw ng hindi nakikitang ultraviolet (UV) at infrared light. Nakakasira ito sa retina cells mo, kaya napakasama ng pagtitig sa araw!
copy.bis: Ang adlaw mogawas og dili makita nga ultraviolet (UV) ug infrared light. Makadaot kini sa imong retina cells, mao nga grabe ka daotan ang pagtutok sa adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is warmer when the Sun is up during the day, and cooler at night!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions day and night and the Sun's presence, but does not demonstrate Earth's rotation on its axis using a globe or explain the cause of day and night.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is warmer when the Sun is up during the day, and cooler at night!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card only links the Sun to daytime warmth; it does not describe the Sun's composition, size, or main radiated energy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is warmer when the Sun is up during the day, and cooler at night!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card makes a general day/night temperature observation but does not involve observing, recording, or describing local weather types and patterns.

copy.en:
Why is it warmer during the day and cooler at night?

It is warmer when the Sun is up during the day, and cooler at night!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mainit kapag araw at mas malamig kapag gabi?

Mas mainit kapag sumisikat ang Araw sa araw, at mas malamig kapag gabi!
copy.bis:
Nganong mas init kon adlaw ug mas bugnaw kon gabii?

Mas init kon misubang ang Adlaw sa adlaw, ug mas bugnaw kon gabii!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun warms land and water unevenly!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make suggestions about the importance of the Sun to living things for a group or class discussion and confirm and record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how uneven solar heating creates wind and that weather depends on sunlight. It does not address the importance of the Sun to living things, nor does it involve making suggestions for a class discussion or referring to secondary sources. The content is only tangentially related to the Sun's role.

copy.en:
How does the Sun make the wind blow?

The Sun warms land and water unevenly! This uneven heating creates wind, meaning our weather depends on sunlight reaching Earth.
copy.tl:
Paano ginagawa ng Araw ang hangin?

Pinapainit ng Araw ang lupa at tubig nang hindi pantay! Gumagawa ito ng hangin, kaya ang panahon ay nakadepende sa sikat ng araw.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa Adlaw sa hangin?

Gipainit sa Adlaw ang yuta ug tubig nga dili parehas! Nagbuhat kini ug hangin, mao nga ang panahon nagsalig sa kahayag sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sunbird is better at pollinating flowers, while the flowerpecker is better at spreading plant seeds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sunbird is better at pollinating flowers, while the flowerpecker is better at spreading plant seeds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not how living things depend on one another to meet their basic needs.

copy.en: The sunbird is better at pollinating flowers, while the flowerpecker is better at spreading plant seeds.
copy.tl: Ang sunbird ay mas mahusay sa pagpopolen ng bulaklak, samantalang ang flowerpecker ay mas mahusay sa pagkalat ng buto ng halaman.
copy.bis: Ang sunbird mas maayo sa pagpolen sa bulak, samtang ang flowerpecker mas maayo sa pagsabwag sa liso sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a sundial's shadow gets faint and hard to read
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses shadow clarity on hazy/cloudy days, but does not describe changes in the direction or length of shadows from a shadow stick, nor does it use such changes to infer why the Sun changes position during a day.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: On hazy or cloudy days
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions cloudy/hazy conditions, which relate to cloud cover as a weather characteristic, but it does not identify or describe basic weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, or cloud cover as a measurable weather feature.

copy.en: On hazy or cloudy days, a sundial's shadow gets faint and hard to read. The shadow is clearest when the sky is bright and the sun shines strong!
copy.tl: Kapag mahamog o makulimlim, ang anino sa sundial ay nagiging malabo at mahirap basahin. Pinakamalinaw ang anino kapag maaliwalas at matingkad ang araw!
copy.bis: Kon mahamog o makulimlim, ang landong sa sundial mahimong dili klaro ug lisod basahon. Pinakaklaro ang landong kon hayag ang langit ug kusog ang adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sundial's design changes depending on where you are on Earth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how sundial gnomon angle varies with latitude, not how Earth's tilt relative to its orbit affects sunlight intensity over a year. No mention of tilt, seasons, or intensity of sunlight.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sundial's design changes depending on where you are on Earth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sundials and location but does not describe changes in shadow direction/length from a shadow stick or infer the Sun's daily position change. It is about gnomon angle by latitude, not daily shadow patterns.

copy.en: A sundial's design changes depending on where you are on Earth! In the Philippines near the equator, the gnomon angle is different from faraway countries.
copy.tl: Iba-iba ang tamang disenyo ng sundial depende kung nasaan ka sa Mundo! Sa Pilipinas malapit sa ekwador, iba ang anggulo ng gnomon kumpara sa malalayong bansa.
copy.bis: Lahi-lahi ang saktong disenyo sa sundial depende asa ka sa Kalibutan! Sa Pilipinas duol sa ekwador, lahi ang anggulo sa gnomon kumpara sa layo nga mga nasod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It’s an old clock that uses a stick's shadow in sunlight! The shadow moves as the Earth rotates to show the time of day.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a stick's shadow and that it moves, but it does not describe changes in the direction and length of shadows or use such changes to infer why the Sun appears to change position during a day. The explanation attributes shadow movement to Earth's rotation, which is not the specific competency skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The shadow moves as the Earth rotates to show the time of day.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Earth's rotation and shadow movement, but it does not demonstrate rotation using a globe or explain day and night. The focus is on sundial timekeeping, not on the globe-based demonstration of Earth's rotation causing day and night.

copy.en:
How does a sundial tell time?

It’s an old clock that uses a stick's shadow in sunlight! The shadow moves as the Earth rotates to show the time of day.
copy.tl:
Paano nagsasabi ng oras ang sundial?

Ito ay lumang orasan na gumagamit ng anino ng patpat sa araw! Gumagalaw ang anino habang umiikot ang mundo para ipakita ang oras.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagsulti sa takna ang sundial?

Kini karaan nga orasan nga naggamit sa landong sa sungkod sa adlaw! Molihok ang landong samtang nagatuyok ang kalibutan para ipakita ang takna.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sundial is one of the earliest clocks! It tells time by where the shadow of an upright part falls on a marked plate.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a shadow stick (upright part) and shadow position, but does not describe changes in direction and length of shadows or infer why the Sun changes position. It only states that a sundial tells time by shadow position, which is related background but not direct instruction for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How did people tell time before clocks?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how natural objects in the sky affect activities of people
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that a sundial was used to tell time, which is an example of a natural object (the Sun) affecting an activity of people. However, it does not explain how the Sun affects activities; it only states the fact that a sundial uses the Sun's shadow. This is related but not direct support for explaining how natural objects in the sky affect activities.

copy.en:
How did people tell time before clocks?

A sundial is one of the earliest clocks! It tells time by where the shadow of an upright part falls on a marked plate.
copy.tl:
Paano nagsabi ng oras ang mga tao bago ang mga orasan?

Ang sundial ay isa sa pinakaunang orasan! Nagsasabi ito ng oras batay sa kung saan tumatama ang anino ng patayong bahagi sa minarkahang plato.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsulti sa oras sa mga tawo sa dili pa ang mga orasan?

Ang sundial usa sa labing unang orasan! Nagsulti kini sa oras base sa kung asa motama ang landong sa tul-id nga bahin sa minarkahan nga plato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It blocks sunlight to form a shadow that points to the time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a sundial's gnomon casts a shadow indicating time. It does not describe changes in shadow direction or length over a day, nor use such changes to infer the Sun's changing position, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The upright, pointed part of a sundial that casts a shadow is called the gnomon! It blocks sunlight to form a shadow that points to the time.
copy.tl: Ang nakatayong bahagi ng sundial na gumagawa ng anino ay tinatawag na gnomon! Hinaharang nito ang sikat ng araw para mabuo ang anino na tumuturo sa oras.
copy.bis: Ang nagtindog nga bahin sa sundial nga maghimo og landong gitawag ug gnomon! Gisagang niini ang adlaw aron motungha ang landong nga magtudlo sa oras.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It tilts toward the north so the shadow matches the Sun's real path
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a sundial gnomon is tilted for accurate timekeeping, but does not describe changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick, nor does it use such observations to infer the Sun's changing position. It shares the topic of shadows and the Sun but does not directly support the competency's skill.

copy.en:
Why is the gnomon tilted?

It tilts toward the north so the shadow matches the Sun's real path, making the time more accurate!
copy.tl:
Bakit nakatagilid ang gnomon?

Nakatagilid ito sa hilaga para tumugma ang anino sa tunay na galaw ng araw, kaya mas tumpak ang oras!
copy.bis:
Nganong nagharag ang gnomon?

Nagharag kini sa amihan aron motakdo ang landong sa tinuod nga agi sa adlaw, busa mas tukma ang oras!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sundials need sunlight to make shadows!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that sundials need sunlight to make shadows and cannot work at night or on cloudy days. It does not describe changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick, nor does it use such changes to infer why the Sun changes position during a day.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sundials need sunlight to make shadows!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sunlight and shadows but does not describe sources of light or their use in everyday situations. A sundial's need for sunlight is only a peripheral example, not direct instruction on light sources and their uses.

copy.en: Sundials need sunlight to make shadows! They cannot work at night or on cloudy days when the Sun is hiding.
copy.tl: Kailangan ng sundial ng sikat ng araw para gumawa ng anino! Hindi ito gagana sa gabi o kapag maulap.
copy.bis: Nagkinahanglan ang sundial ug silaw sa adlaw aron mohimo ug landong! Dili kini molihok kon gabii o madag-um.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the travel time of sunlight, which is a fact about the Sun–Earth distance and speed of light. G4-E-7 requires describing the Sun's composition, size, or main radiated energy. The card does not address any of these characteristics, so it is only topically related to the Sun.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system, naming major celestial objects, and their main features and composition. The card only gives a single fact about sunlight travel time; it does not describe the solar system's structure, celestial objects, or their features/composition. Thus it is only related to the Sun as a celestial object.

copy.en:
How long does it take for sunlight to reach us?

It travels super fast! Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal bago marating sa atin ang liwanag ng Araw?

Sobrang bilis ng biyahe nito! Mga 8 minuto ang inaabot ng liwanag ng Araw bago marating ang Lupa.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay ang abuton sa kahayag sa Adlaw aron makaabot kanato?

Dali kaayo ang biyahe niini! Mga 8 ka minuto ang abuton sa kahayag sa Adlaw aron makaabot sa Yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Clouds block some sunlight! This changes how warm the day feels for us and our crops.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make suggestions about the importance of the Sun to living things for a group or class discussion and confirm and record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that clouds block sunlight and affect warmth for people and crops, touching on the Sun's importance to living things. However, the competency requires making suggestions for a group/class discussion and confirming/recording ideas from secondary sources. The card provides a simple factual explanation without any suggestion-making, discussion, or source-referencing activity, so it does not directly support the competency's action.

copy.en:
Why do weather reports talk about clouds and sunshine?

Clouds block some sunlight! This changes how warm the day feels for us and our crops.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagbabalita ang ulat ng panahon tungkol sa ulap at araw?

Humaharang ang ulap sa sikat ng araw! Nagbabago nito ang init ng araw para sa atin at sa mga pananim.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagbalita ang weather report bahin sa panganod ug adlaw?

Mo-block ang panganod sa adlaw! Nag-usab niini ang kainit sa adlaw para kanato ug sa mga tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Place seed pots in a sunny spot but avoid direct afternoon sun
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about planting seeds and sunlight conditions for seed growth. G6-E-5 concerns interpreting PHIVOLCS volcano monitoring alert levels and actions before/during/after a volcanic eruption. There is no connection to volcanic activity or safety.

copy.en: A mother tamaraw usually has just one calf at a time, so their numbers grow very slowly.
copy.tl: Karaniwang nag-aanak ang inahing tamaraw ng iisang guya lang, kaya mabagal dumami ang kanilang lahi.
copy.bis: Ang inahang tamaraw kasagaran manganak ug usa ra ka nati, mao nga hinay modaghan ang ilang kaliwat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tamarind's sweet-sour taste comes from tartaric acid in its pulp!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions tartaric acid as the cause of tamarind's sourness, but does not address identifying solutions, litmus indicators, or classifying acids/bases/salts. copy.en:
Why is tamarind so sour?

Tamarind's sweet-sour taste comes from tartaric acid in its pulp! It's used to flavor sinigang and other Filipino dishes.
copy.tl:
Bakit maasim ang sampalok?

Ang tamis-asim na lasa ng sampalok ay galing sa tartaric acid na nasa pulp nito! Ginagamit ito sa sinigang at iba pang lutuing Pilipino.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga aslom ang sampalok?

Ang tam-is-aslom nga lasa sa sampalok gikan sa tartaric acid sa pulp niini! Gigamit kini sa sinigang ug uban pang putahe sa Pilipinas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plants with one big main root have a taproot system
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that water is one of the basic needs of plants and animals
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains taproot and fibrous root systems. It does not address water as a basic need of plants and animals, nor any Earth/space content such as soils, weather, or the Sun.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plants with one big main root have a taproot system
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant root morphology, not landforms, bodies of water, or their influence on living and non-living components. No connection to the competency's subject.

copy.en:
Why do some plants have one big root while others have many thin roots?

Plants with one big main root have a taproot system, while plants with many spreading thin roots have a fibrous root system.
copy.tl:
Bakit may mga halamang may isang malaking ugat habang ang iba naman ay maraming manipis na ugat?

Ang mga halamang may isang malaking pangunahing ugat ay may taproot system, habang ang mga halamang may maraming kumakalat na manipis na ugat ay may fibrous root system.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang uban nga mga tanom adunay usa ka dako nga gamot samtang ang uban adunay daghang nipis nga mga gamot?

Ang mga tanom nga adunay usa ka dako nga pangunang gamot adunay taproot system, samtang ang mga tanom nga adunay daghang nagkatag nga nipis nga mga gamot adunay fibrous root system.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states what tardigrades eat but does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources to classify. It only provides a feeding fact, not the grouping skill.

The mouth reference is incidental, not a direct teaching of the competency.

copy.en:
What do tardigrades eat?

Most tardigrades pierce plant cells, algae, or tiny animals with their mouths and suck the fluid out.
copy.tl:
Ano ang kinakain ng tardigrade?

Karamihan sa mga tardigrade ay tumutusok ng selula ng halaman, algae, o maliliit na hayop at sinisipsip ang laman nito.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gikaon sa tardigrade?

Kadaghanan sa mga tardigrade nagatusok sa mga selula sa tanom, algae, o gagmayng mananap ug nagasuyop sa sulod niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: lessening damage from radiation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes and discuss some of the factors that cause mutations, such as infectious agents, radiation, and chemicals
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions radiation as a damaging factor but does not describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes, nor does it discuss mutation causes. It focuses on a protective protein, not on mutations themselves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: wraps around the tardigrade's DNA
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions DNA as the target of protection. It does not explain the role of DNA, genes, or chromosomes in the transmission of traits.

copy.en:
How do tardigrades survive radiation?

A special protein wraps around the tardigrade's DNA like a shield, lessening damage from radiation — so less harm happens inside them than in other animals.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakaligtas ang tardigrade sa radiation?

May espesyal na protina na bumabalot sa DNA ng tardigrade parang panangga, na binabawasan ang pinsala mula sa radiation — kaya mas kaunti ang nasisira sa loob nito kumpara sa ibang hayop.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkaluwas sa tardigrade sa radiation?

Adunay espesyal nga protina nga moputos sa DNA sa tardigrade nga morag taming, nga makapakunhod sa kadaot gikan sa radiation — mao nga gamay ra ang madaot sulod niini kumpara sa ubang mananap.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: until water returns
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water as a trigger for revival but does not teach that water is a basic need of all living things. It focuses on tardigrade dormancy, not on identifying air, food, water, or shelter as needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a dried tardigrade can stay "asleep" for many years until water returns
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a survival adaptation (cryptobiosis) but does not use secondary sources or describe how animals changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. It is a factual example of dormancy, not an explanation of evolutionary adaptation.

copy.en:
How long can a dried tardigrade "sleep"?

In the tun form, a dried tardigrade can stay "asleep" for many years until water returns — then it slowly soaks up water and starts moving again within minutes to hours.
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal makatulog ang tuyong tardigrade?

Sa anyong tun, kayang manatiling 'tulog' ang tardigrade nang maraming taon hanggang bumalik ang tubig — pag nabasa muli, dahan-dahan itong sumisipsip ng tubig at gumagalaw ulit sa loob ng ilang minuto hanggang oras.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay makatulog ang uga nga tardigrade?

Sa porma nga tun, makahimo ang uga nga tardigrade nga magpabiling 'natulog' sa daghang tuig hangtod mobalik ang tubig — kon mabasa pag-usab, hinay-hinay kining mosuyop og tubig ug molihok pag-usab sulod sa pipila ka minuto hangtod oras.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You need a microscope just to see its eight tiny legs move.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions eight tiny legs moving but does not describe outer body parts or identify their role in movement or food gathering, which is the focus of G3-L-4.

copy.en:
How small is a tardigrade really?

Usually less than a millimeter — about the size of a pen dot or a grain of sand! You need a microscope just to see its eight tiny legs move.
copy.tl:
Gaano kaliit talaga ang tardigrade?

Karaniwang mas maliit pa sa milimetro — kasinliit ng tuldok ng panulat o butil ng buhangin! Kailangan mo ng mikroskopyo para makita ang walong paa nitong gumagalaw.
copy.bis:
Unsa kagamay gyud ang tardigrade?

Kasagaran mas gamay pa sa usa ka milimetro — sama kagamay sa tuldok sa bolpen o lugas sa balas! Kinahanglan nimo ang mikroskopyo aron makita ang walo ka tiil niini nga naglihok.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card presents an exception to the need for water rather than teaching that water is a basic need of all living things. It does not directly support identifying basic needs such as air, food, water, and shelter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a dried-up tardigrade can stay alive for years with no water, then come back to life once it gets wet again
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a survival ability but does not frame it as an example of animals changing to better suit their environment, nor does it mention mimicry, camouflage, or adaptation through change. It is only tangentially related to environmental adaptation.

copy.en:
Can an animal survive years without water?

Yes — a dried-up tardigrade can stay alive for years with no water, then come back to life once it gets wet again!
copy.tl:
Kaya bang mabuhay ng hayop nang walang tubig sa loob ng taon?

Oo! Sa anyong tuyo, ang tardigrade ay nananatiling buhay nang ilang taon na walang tubig, at nabubuhay muli kapag nabasa!
copy.bis:
Makahimo ba og hayop nga mabuhi nga walay tubig sulod sa mga tuig?

Oo! Sa uga nga porma, ang tardigrade mabuhi og daghang tuig nga walay tubig, ug mabuhi pag-usab kung mabasa!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food and water but does not teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It focuses on survival without food/water, not on identifying basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: by entering a deep sleep called cryptobiosis

assignedReviews.reason: Cryptobiosis is a survival adaptation, but the card does not describe how the animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it use secondary sources. It is only loosely related to adaptation examples like mimicry or camouflage.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: by entering a deep sleep called cryptobiosis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a survival state, not the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Cryptobiosis is not presented as a response or growth/reproduction characteristic.

copy.en:
How long can a tardigrade survive without food?

A tardigrade, or 'water bear,' can survive up to 30 years without food or water by entering a deep sleep called cryptobiosis.
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal mabubuhay ang tardigrade na walang pagkain?

Ang tardigrade o water bear ay maaaring mabuhay nang hanggang 30 taon nang walang pagkain o tubig sa pamamagitan ng malalim na pagtulog na tinatawag na cryptobiosis.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay makasugakod ang tardigrade nga walay pagkaon?

Ang tardigrade o water bear makasugakod hangtod 30 ka tuig nga walay pagkaon o tubig pinaagi sa lawom nga pagkatulog nga gitawag og cryptobiosis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it can survive extreme heat, cold, and even no water at all
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a tardigrade's current survival abilities but does not explain how the animal has changed or evolved to better suit its environment, nor does it mention mimicry, camouflage, or use of secondary sources. It only touches on the same broad topic of animal-environment fit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: survive extreme heat, cold, and even no water at all
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions surviving without water, which relates to basic needs, but it does not identify the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter) or teach that these are needs. It only notes that tardigrades can survive without water, which is an exception rather than a lesson on basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you need a microscope to see it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that a microscope is needed to see the tardigrade, but it does not teach that some organisms are unicellular and others multicellular, nor does it classify tardigrades as either. The microscope mention is incidental and does not support the competency's core concept.

copy.en:
What tiny creature can survive almost anything?

The tardigrade, or water bear! It's so small you need a microscope to see it, yet it can survive extreme heat, cold, and even no water at all.
copy.tl:
Anong napakaliit na hayop ang halos hindi nasisira?

Ang tardigrade o water bear! Napakaliit nito kaya mikroskopyo lang ang makakakita, pero kaya nitong mabuhay sa matinding init, lamig, at kahit walang tubig.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga gamay kaayo nga mananap ang halos dili madaot?

Ang tardigrade o water bear! Gamay kaayo kini nga mikroskopyo ra ang makakita, apan makasugakod kini sa hilabihang kainit, katugnaw, ug bisan walay tubig.

copy.bis: Mokupot pag-ayo ang nating tarsier sa balahibo sa iyang inahan, o dad-on kini sa inahan gamit ang baba.

copy.en: Besides its big eyes, the tarsier also uses sharp hearing to find and catch insects in the dark.
copy.tl: Bukod sa malalaking mata, gumagamit din ang tarsier ng matalas na pandinig para mahuli ang insekto sa dilim.
copy.bis: Gawas sa dagkong mata, gigamit sab sa tarsier ang hait nga pandungog aron madakpan ang insekto sa kangitngit.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes taste bud renewal but never mentions cell division, mitosis, meiosis, or the role of mitosis in growth and repair. It is an example of a biological renewal process but does not directly teach the competency's required concepts.

copy.en: Your taste buds don't last forever — old ones die off and new ones grow back every few days or weeks!
copy.tl: Hindi tumatagal magpakailanman ang mga taste buds mo — namamatay ang luma at may bagong tumutubo tuwing ilang araw o linggo!
copy.bis: Dili molungtad hangtod sa hangtod ang imong mga taste buds — mamatay ang daan ug motubo ang bag-o matag pipila ka adlaw o semana!
